label: sprites/fw_steam.spr: a steam puff that rises and thins, animated

R1.reason: Reads as a steam wisp that rises and thins: a grey column that is dense low down in frames 1 to 5, then breaks up and fades through frames 6 to 11. It is a steam effect as the brief asks. It is a thin column rather than a full puff, but that is about shape, scored under R2.

R2.reason: The frames are 64 by 64 and the border is clean (border max 0.24, mean 0.001), so the size is right. But the effect fills only a narrow strip, about a fifth of each frame's width, down the middle-left of the cell. In frames 2 to 7 its base is cut off at the bottom edge of the cell. It does not fill the frame as a steam puff should.

R3.reason: The colour is a dim, low-contrast grey on the near-black background, and in the additive blend most frames barely show. Frames 0, 10 and 11 are nearly empty. Half-Life's steam sprites read as a clearly lighter grey-white. The colour is too faint to match by eye.

R4.reason: The measures pass: 12 frames, the envelope peaks at 0.27 with first and last frames at 0, and the border is clean. But the rise the brief asks for is not visible. In frames 2 to 7 the base of the column stays at the same height in each cell, so it reads as flickering in place rather than rising.

R5.reason: The name fw_steam and the additive format are right. The type is parallel, not parallel oriented, which is the type Half-Life's steam sprite (steam1) uses per the amendment on the slot's type and format. That is a fault against R5 by measure.
